text: HAL has agreed to take half a company. The price: zero rupees.
The company is HATSOFF. It trains military and civil helicopter pilots, on simulators.
Until now, it was a fifty fifty joint venture: HAL and Canada's CAE.
Last year's turnover: eighty point nine five crore rupees.
CAE's half: three crore eighty four lakh shares, ten rupees each. That's about thirty eight crore of share capital.
HAL's price for it: nil. HAL says it wants full management control.
So why would CAE walk away with nothing? The filing doesn't say. Back to the napkin: half a company, zero rupees.
